syllabusTopics: Motion of a freely falling body
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9 (extra unit card). Exam bank: definitions (2024), 200 m stone drop (2023), car acceleration (2023).

card.title: Exam bank — every board question on kinematics

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three questions: define position/velocity/acceleration (2024), stone dropped 200 m (2023: ~6.3 s, ~63 m/s impact), car 10 m/s at 2 m/s2 for 4 s (2023: 18 m/s, 56 m). Uniform-acceleration equations plus free-fall specials (t = sqrt(2h/g), v = sqrt(2gh)) cover everything.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: v = u + at · s = ut + half at2 · v2 = u2 + 2as · free fall: t = sqrt(2h/g), v = sqrt(2gh) · projectile R = u2 sin2theta/g

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Motion equations need UNIFORM acceleration (meaning constant slope on v-t graphs). Free-fall specials need u = 0 and negligible air. Definitions must separate instantaneous (slope/tangent) from average (chord/total).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Stone 200 m, g = 10: t = sqrt(40) ~ 6.3 s, v = 63 m/s. Car: v = 10 + 8 = 18 m/s, s = 40 + 16 = 56 m. Relative velocity flips with observer. Complementary launch angles share range.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): h = half g t2 gives t = sqrt(2x200/10) ~ 6.3 s; v = gt ~ 63 m/s. Companion: v = u + at = 18 m/s; s = ut + half at2 = 56 m. NEB 2024 (2): position (where), velocity (rate of position), acceleration (rate of velocity).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: g = 10 vs 9.8 mixing within one solution; air resistance ignored silently in projectile symmetry; variable acceleration forced into uniform formulas.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Graphical treatment: v-t area gives displacement, slope gives acceleration — the equations read off the graphs. Projectile range derives from x-y separation with landing condition y = 0.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Free-fall numbers: sqrt(2h/g), sqrt(2gh). v-t area = displacement, slope = acceleration — faster than formulas for staged motion. 45 degrees max range; complementary angles equal range.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (2): define position, velocity, acceleration. NEB 2023 (3): 200 m stone drop (time + impact v). NEB 2023 (3): car 10 m/s, a = 2, 4 s (final v + distance). NEB 2022 (5): horizontal projectile from 80 m tower at 20 m/s (t = 4 s, R = 80 m, impact 44.72 m/s at 63.4 degrees). NEB 2022 (4): vertical projection 49 m/s (5 s up, max height, double flight time).
